transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not overreacting or wasting your time—it's probably just normal work stress—but I'm mostly here because my sleep has gotten really unreliable lately. 

Even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I just lie there... replaying sales forecasts and little team issues in my head. And then I'll wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and I just can't get my brain to power down again. I'm sorry, I hope I'm explaining that clearly enough. Is that the sort of thing you usually help people with?
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things outside of work as well?

Um... I guess a little bit? I mean, I try really hard to keep it together, so I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about normal adult responsibilities. But... yeah, most days my mind just kind of jumps around. 

Like, I'll be worrying about whether we'll hit our launch numbers, and then suddenly I'm stressing over whether someone on my team is about to quit. And then it just bleeds into other things, like... paying the mortgage, or a client renewal. It just sort of feels like every small delay could turn into something major. I know everyone has bills and work stress, though, so I hope I'm not being too dramatic about it. Does that answer what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge during the day, not just when you're thinking about specific worries?

Um, yeah, I guess I do. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm just constantly complaining, but... I do feel kind of wound up almost all the time. It's like... even when I'm just at home, you know, trying to eat dinner or something, my body feels like I'm sitting right in the middle of a high-pressure pipeline review. 

And my shoulders... they're just always tight. I try to relax them, I really do, but they just stay tense. It's probably just from sitting at a desk all day, right? I hope it's okay that I'm mentioning that—I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the details you need. Is that the kind of feeling you meant?
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I've never had a sudden wave of fear just hit me out of nowhere like that. It's really more of just a... a steady, constant hum of stress, like I was saying before. 

I hope that's okay? Like, I don't want to make my situation sound worse than it actually is, and I definitely don't have those intense peaks you're describing. I hope I'm not wasting your time since I don't have that... is it helpful that I just have the regular kind of worry? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you usually lie awake at night because you're worrying about something specific?

Um... yeah, I guess that does happen. I mean, I really try to practice good sleep hygiene, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just staring at my phone all night. But... yeah, my sleep has gotten pretty unreliable lately. 

Even when I'm completely exhausted and I get into bed, I just... I lie there and my brain starts replaying all the sales forecasts and little issues with my team. And then, even if I do fall asleep, I usually wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning. And once I'm awake, I just can't get my brain to power down again. It's probably just normal work stress keeping me up, right? I hope it's okay that I'm bringing it up... I just want to make sure I'm answering your question properly. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you think your worrying is what's causing you to wake up in the middle of the night?

Um, yeah, I really think it is the worrying. I mean, I try so hard to just shut it off, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just letting myself spiral on purpose. I'll literally lie there and tell myself, "Brenda, you've done the plan, everything is fine, just let it go." And I try to be good about it! 

But then... maybe five minutes later, I'm just right back in another loop. I'll finally resolve one concern in my head, and then it's like three more just pop up to take its place. It's so frustrating because I know I should be sleeping, and I'm trying to be disciplined about it. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely neurotic or anything? I just... I really can't seem to control it once it starts. Is that a normal thing to happen when you're stressed?
Do you usually wake up in the middle of the night with a specific worry on your mind?

Um, well, it's not always one specific thing right away. I mean, sometimes I just wake up and my heart is beating a little fast, and I feel this sort of... generalized dread? 

But then, yeah, almost immediately my brain will latch onto something specific. Usually it's work-related, like, "Did I send that email?" or "What if the quarterly numbers are off?" I really try not to let work bleed into my personal time like that, I swear I do. I know how important work-life balance is. It's just... once I'm awake, it's like my brain goes searching for something to fixate on. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm not trying to be difficult or vague, it's just sometimes hard to pinpoint exactly what wakes me up versus what I start thinking about *after* I'm awake. Am I explaining that okay?
Is there something in particular that's been stressing you out more than other things lately?

Um... well, it's not really just one specific thing, which I know probably sounds unhelpful. I wish it was just one thing, because then I could just tackle it and fix it, you know? I really do try to stay on top of everything, and I promise I'm usually very organized. But lately... most days my mind just sort of jumps around from one thing to another. 

Like, I'll be worrying about whether we'll hit the new launch numbers, and then suddenly I'm stressing over whether someone on my team is about to quit. And then it shifts to the mortgage, or an upcoming client renewal. It just feels like every small delay could turn into something major, even when I know logically that's probably not true. I really try not to let it get to me, and I tell myself to just take things one step at a time. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound like I can't handle my responsibilities... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you usually have trouble falling asleep at the beginning of the night, or is it more about waking up in the middle of the night and then having trouble getting back to sleep?

Um... well, it's actually kind of both? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a complete mess. I mean, I really try to have good sleep hygiene—I don't look at my phone in bed, I try to wind down... but lately, it's just gotten so unreliable. 

Even when I go to bed completely exhausted, I'll just lie there replaying all the sales forecasts and team issues from the day. I try so hard to just shut it off, but it takes a while to finally drift off. And then, like I was saying, I'll wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning, and I just can't get my brain to power down again. I really am trying my best to manage it, I promise. Is it normal for it to be bad at both ends of the night like that? I just want to make sure I'm explaining this clearly enough for you.
Is there something specific that you think is causing your sleep to be unreliable lately?

Um, no, not really one specific thing. I mean, I wish I could point to just one big event or, like, a major crisis, but honestly... nothing huge has changed recently. 

I feel like I should have a better answer for you, I'm sorry. It's just... everything is generally fine. I'm doing well at work, my team is good. I mean, there's the usual day-to-day stuff, obviously, but nothing I shouldn't be able to handle. I really do think I manage my stress pretty well during the day. It's just... I don't know why my sleep has decided to go off the rails like this. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have a clear reason for it? I just don't want to make it sound like my life is falling apart when it's really not. I'm just struggling a bit with the sleep part right now. Does that make sense?
Is your unreliable sleep related to any particular situation or event in your life?

Um, actually, I think that's pretty much what I was just trying to say... I hope I didn't confuse things earlier? 

But no, there really isn't any one particular situation or event that I can tie it to. Like I said, work is going well, and I'm really trying to keep everything running smoothly. There hasn't been any big upheaval or anything like that. I mean, if there was, I would absolutely tell you, I promise. I want to be as helpful as possible so we can figure this out. 

It just feels like this sleep issue kind of came out of nowhere, even though everything else is pretty much under control. I'm sorry if that's not the kind of answer you're looking for... is it okay that I don't have a specific trigger to point to?
Do you think your worrying is the main reason you're having trouble sleeping?

Um... I guess so? I really hope I don't sound completely neurotic saying this. I mean, I try so hard to just be proactive and stay on top of everything, so I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around panicking all day. 

But... yeah, I suppose my mind does race a lot. Most days it just kind of jumps around. Like, I'll be thinking about whether we'll hit our launch numbers, and then suddenly I'm worrying if someone on my team is about to quit, and then it's on to the mortgage, or an upcoming client renewal... It just feels like every small delay could turn into something major if I'm not careful. 

I really am trying to keep it all in perspective, I promise, and I know it probably sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud. Do you... do you think that kind of thinking is what's keeping me awake? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way so we can figure this out.
Do you usually wake up feeling anxious or worried?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I hope that's a good thing? When I do finally manage to sleep, and I wake up the next morning, I wouldn't say I feel anxious right away. 

Usually, I just feel... tired, honestly. Like I said, I really try to keep everything together during the day, so I think when I wake up, I'm mostly just trying to get my bearings and get ready for work. I want to make sure I'm starting the day off right, you know? 

So, no, I don't think I wake up in a panic or anything like that. I really hope I'm giving you the information you need? I just want to make sure I'm not making things sound worse than they actually are.
Do you think your worrying is primarily focused on work-related issues or does it also encompass other areas of your life?

Um... well, it's mostly work, I think. I mean, work is just such a big part of my life right now, and I really want to do a good job. I don't want you to think I'm completely obsessed or anything, but it's just where my focus has to be, you know? 

I do sometimes think about other things, like... like I mentioned the mortgage earlier, or just general day-to-day stuff. But it's not like I'm sitting around worrying about every little detail of my personal life. I really try to keep things balanced and not let it spill over too much. 

I guess work is just the most demanding part of my day, so it makes sense that it takes up the most space in my head? I hope that makes sense. Is it normal for it to be mostly focused on one area like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what's going on.
Do you think your sleep problems started before or after your worrying began?

Um... gosh, that's a really good question. I'm actually not entirely sure? I really hope it's okay that I don't have an exact timeline for you. I just don't want to give you the wrong answer and mess up your assessment or anything. 

I feel like they kind of just... blend together? Like, I've always tried to be really on top of things and be a high achiever, so maybe the worrying was always there in the background, and then the sleep just started getting worse as work got busier? 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful answer. It's just hard to separate them in my head. Is it normal to not really know which one started first? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
Is your worrying usually about specific problems or is it more of a general feeling of unease?

Um... I guess it's usually about specific things? I really hope I'm explaining this right, I don't want to sound like my thoughts are just all over the place. 

It's just that there are a lot of specific things, if that makes sense? Like, most days my mind kind of jumps around a lot. I'll be thinking about whether we'll actually hit the launch numbers for the quarter, and then suddenly I'm stressing over whether someone on my sales team is about to quit. And then my brain just shifts to, you know, the mortgage, or a big client renewal coming up. 

It just sort of feels like every small delay could turn into something major. I know that probably sounds like I'm overreacting, and I really try to keep it in check so it doesn't affect my work or bother anyone else. But... yeah, it just jumps from one specific problem to the next. Is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
How long have you been experiencing this excessive worrying?

Um... well, it hasn't been forever, I don't think. I mean, I've always been a hard worker and cared about my job, which I think is a good thing, right? But the really intense part, where it feels like it's just constantly jumping from one thing to another... I guess that's been building up for a little over a year now. 

We had this big reorganization in the sales division about thirteen months ago, and I took on a lot more responsibility. I was really grateful for the opportunity, and I didn't want to let anyone down, so I just poured everything into making sure it went smoothly. I think that's when it started getting a bit more difficult to turn my brain off. 

I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining about my job or anything, because I really do love it and I know I'm lucky to be in this position. It's just that since that reorg, the pressure has been a lot higher. Does that timeline make sense to you? I hope thirteen months doesn't sound like I've just been letting this go on for too long without saying anything.
Has your worrying affected your relationships with family or friends?

Um... I guess it has, a little bit? I really hate to admit that, because I always try to be a good partner and a supportive boss. I don't want you to think I'm failing at either of those things. 

But... well, I spend so much time second-guessing my decisions at work that my pipeline reviews have started getting a bit tense. I just want to make sure everything is perfect, you know? But I think it frustrates my team sometimes. And then... by the time I get home, I'm just so drained from it all. I end up being a little reactive, or just not fully present with my husband. 

He's been really understanding, but I feel terrible about it. I should be able to leave work at work and just be a good wife when I get home. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person or anything? I'm really trying to work on it, I just... I don't want to let anyone down, at work or at home. Is it common for this kind of stress to bleed over into relationships like that?
Do you think your sleep problems would improve if you were no longer worrying about work and other things?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I mean, I'd like to think so? I really try to practice good sleep hygiene and do all the things you're supposed to do, like not looking at my phone before bed. I don't want you to think I'm just lying there worrying on purpose instead of trying to sleep. 

But I guess if I wasn't thinking about the pipeline or the team or... everything else... maybe it would be easier to just drift off. I've never really thought about it like that, like one causes the other. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering that right. I just haven't really experienced a time lately where I wasn't worrying, so it's hard to say for sure if the sleep would fix itself. Is that a normal way to feel?
